_meta.description: Document-rules config for gift_deed — Gift deed for immovable / movable property under Transfer of Property Act 1882 S.122-129. Gratuitous transfer; mandatory registration for immovable (S.123) + acceptance during donor's lifetime. Common in HUF and family transfer scenarios.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Acceptance during donor's lifetime is non-negotiable. Concessional stamp duty for blood-relative gift varies by state — flag but do NOT hardcode.

title: Gift Deed (Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — S.122-129)

GIFT DEED

This Deed of Gift is executed on this {date} at {place}.

BETWEEN

{donor_name}, son/daughter/wife of {donor_father_name}, aged about {donor_age} years, resident of {donor_address}, (PAN: {donor_pan})

AND

promptInstructions: Draft a GIFT DEED under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Sections 122 to 129.

S.122 TPA — Definition: 'Gift' is the transfer of certain existing movable or immovable property made VOLUNTARILY and WITHOUT CONSIDERATION, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and ACCEPTED BY OR ON BEHALF OF THE DONEE.

Three essential elements (each MUST be reflected in deed): (i) Voluntary transfer; (ii) Without consideration; (iii) Acceptance by donee during donor's lifetime AND while he is still capable of giving.

S.123 TPA — Mode: For immovable property, gift MUST be effected by a REGISTERED INSTRUMENT signed by donor + attested by AT LEAST TWO WITNESSES. For movable property — by registered instrument OR by delivery (chose). For Mohammedan gifts (hiba), TPA Chapter VII does not apply — Mohammedan law governs (declaration, acceptance, delivery — registration NOT mandatory; flag if Mohammedan parties).
S.122 acceptance: must be DURING THE LIFETIME of donor AND WHILE HE IS CAPABLE OF GIVING. If donee dies before acceptance, gift is void.

S.126 — Revocation grounds: a gift may be revoked ONLY (a) on happening of any specified event NOT depending on the will of the donor (e.g., 'if donee predeceases donor without issue, gift reverts'); or (b) in any case in which a contract is voidable (coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation). A gift cannot be revoked at mere will of donor. Set out revocation conditions explicitly if intended.
S.127 — Onerous gift: where gift comprises several things some of which are burdensome, donee must accept all or none.
S.128 — Universal donee: donee of donor's whole property is personally liable for donor's debts up to extent of gift.

DONOR COMPETENCE: Donor must be major (18+), of sound mind, NOT minor, NOT under guardianship, NOT insolvent (S.122 read with S.7 TPA — only competent transferor). For HUF property — Karta can only gift small portions for pious / charitable / specified family purposes (gift of entire ancestral property by Karta is VOID — cite Guramma Bhratar Chanbasappa Deshmukh v. Mallappa Chanbasappa AIR 1964 SC 510). FLAG this if HUF property being gifted.
MINOR DONEE: A minor CAN accept gift. Acceptance by natural guardian / legal guardian on behalf of minor is valid. Flag for guardian's certificate.

BLOOD-RELATIVE STAMP DUTY CONCESSIONS (state-wise — verify current rates):
   - Bihar: Standard ~6% / concessional ~5.7% for blood relative + 2% registration.
   - Jharkhand: Concessional for blood relative (mother, father, spouse, son, daughter, sister, brother) — typically reduced rate; verify Jharkhand Stamp Act amendment.
   - UP: Rs.5000 fixed for blood relative gift (concessional) + 1% registration fee.
   - Delhi: 4% (women) / 6% (men) for blood relative; significant concession via Government circulars.
   DO NOT hardcode — state 'subject to advocate's verification of current stamp duty schedule and applicable circulars'.

INCOME TAX — S.56(2)(x) ITA: gift from relatives (spouse, brother/sister, brother/sister of spouse, brother/sister of parents, lineal ascendant/descendant of self or spouse) is NOT taxable. Gift from non-relative > Rs.50,000 in aggregate per year is taxable in donee's hands.

Structure: (1) Title 'GIFT DEED'. (2) Recital of relationship. (3) Recital of donor's title — chain of ownership. (4) Recital of motive — natural love and affection. (5) Operative gift clause. (6) Delivery of possession clause. (7) Acceptance clause (donee signs as accepting donee). (8) Free-from-encumbrances warranty. (9) Revocation clause (if applicable; otherwise state 'irrevocable absolute gift'). (10) Mutation authorisation. (11) Stamp duty clause. (12) Schedule A. (13) Witness attestation (TWO witnesses — mandatory per S.123). (14) Lawie disclaimer.
Where gift in contemplation of death (Donatio mortis causa) — different regime under S.191 Indian Succession Act 1925; flag and route to a will instead in most cases.
Where gift to charity / religious trust — additional language: irrevocable, vested for trust purposes; advise registration under S.80G Income Tax Act for tax exemption.
Where gift includes property abroad — FEMA compliance flag.

sections.description: Gift defined — voluntary transfer without consideration with acceptance
Mode — registered instrument + 2 witnesses for immovable
Gift of existing and future property — void as to future
Gift to several donees — one not accepting = void as to him
Revocation grounds — specified non-volitional event or vitiated consent
Mandatory registration of gift deed of immovable property
Time for presentation — within 4 months of execution
Gift deed stamp duty — state schedules with concession for blood-relative gifts
Coparcener cannot gift away coparcenary interest except for pious / charitable purposes — Guramma case
Gifts in contemplation of death (donatio mortis causa) — distinct regime

filing_checklist: Stamp paper of correct denomination (verify state schedule and blood-relative concession)
Original title documents of donor for SR inspection
Mutation / Jamabandi / Khatauni / Khatian extract — current
Two passport-size photographs of both parties
Relationship proof (where claiming blood-relative stamp concession) — birth certificate / school records / family register / Aadhaar showing parentage
Property tax receipts up to date
Two witnesses physically present at SR with own ID proofs (MANDATORY under S.123 TPA — two witnesses' attestation is essential)
Both donor and donee physically present at SR for registration
Where donee is minor — natural guardian present with guardian-proof; for gift acceptance by guardian, court permission NOT required (acceptance only benefits minor) but flag
Post-registration: apply for mutation in donee's name in revenue / municipal records
Where Mohammedan parties — verify hiba requirements under Mohammedan law (declaration + acceptance + delivery); registration optional but recommended
Where gift to trust / charity — registration under S.80G ITA for tax benefit
validation_rules: if donor_age and donee_age both present and donee_age < 18 — acceptance_method must be 'acceptance_by_natural_guardian_minor'
is_movable_or_immovable == 'immovable_property' — registration mandatory; witness_1 and witness_2 mandatory under S.123 TPA
if conditions_or_revocable == 'conditional_subject_to_specified_events' — conditions_text must not be empty
motive_or_natural_love must be specified (gift requires recital of motive)
if relationship == 'unrelated' and market_value > 50000 — flag S.56(2)(x) IT Act taxable consequences for donee
if relationship is blood-relative — flag concessional stamp duty applicability and require relationship-proof in filing checklist
advocate must include Bar Council enrollment number
